pages.text: 7 Canada: Tobacco Taxation and the Tobacco Products Act GETTING TOUGH ON TOBACCO Smoking is a leading cause of death among Canadians. The Issue Cigarette smoke can also be hazardous to non-smokers. While the shift in public opinion supporting non- smoking has been evident since about 1980, stronger measures have recently been implemented in order to protect non-smckers from smoke, to encourage smokers to quit, and to encourage non-smokers to remain smoke-free. Two federal government policies have had an impact on smokers and on tobacco companies. These are tobacco taxation and tobacco advertising controls. The Policies Taxes on tobacco have increased with every federal . budget since the late 1980s. For example, recent Taxation increases in tobacco taxes added 86¢ to a pack of cigarettes in B.C. Smokers now pay close to $5.00 for a pack of 20 cigarettes. Research that connects tobacco to disease, along with expressed public opinion against smoking, has encouraged legislators to tax tobacco extensively. There is some evidence that high tobacco prices encourage people to stop smoking. While taxation targets the consumer, the 1989 Tobacco Advertising Controls Products Control Act targets tobacco advertising and = its association with the “good life.” The Act phases out advertising and places increased restrictions on the promotion of cigarettes and tobacco. All trademark advertising is to end as of January 1993. While the Act is being appealed in the courts by the tobacco companies, the Act’s restrictions remain in force until the appeal procedure is completed.

pages.text: CANADA LIBRARY OF PARLIAMENT BIBLIOTHEQUE DU PARLEMENT TOBACCO SMOKING* ISSUE DEFINITION Over the past two or three decades, North America has witnessed a revolution in attitudes towards tobacco smoking. What was once considered a normal habit has become increasingly socially unacceptable. An ever-growing number of non-smokers are much less tolerant of smoking, and anti-smoking activists have become very vocal in their opposition to the habit. Governments and other organizations are more receptive to lobbying efforts and are introducing bans and restrictions on smoking. Since the 1960s, research has documented the health hazards of tobacco smoking. Originally, the emphasis was on the danger to the smoker, but it has become clear in recent years that non-smokers are also at risk from inhaling second-hand or "“sidestream" smoke. While most experts and governments accept the scientific and medical evidence of the dangers of tobacco smoke, changes do not come easily. Both the Surgeon General in the United States and the Royal Society of Canada have concluded that tobacco is a highly addictive~-product and many smokers find it difficult, if not impossible, to stop smoking, even if they want to. Tobacco manufactuers, who refuse to acknowledge that any health risks have been proved to be associated with their product, are a powerful group. The economic well-being of tobacco farmers must also be considered. In the past, Government policies were somewhat ambivalent; significant tax revenues are derived from tobacco, yet governments are increasingly concerned about the rising costs of treating the preventable illnesses that result from tobacco use. pages.text: 2012 Ontario Budget Tobacco Enforcement Tobacco use continues to be the leading cause of preventable disease and premature death in Ontario. The government’s Smoke-Free Ontario Strategy has made the province a leader in tobacco control. Ontario remains committed to reducing smoking among youth and other vulnerable persons, and to achieving the lowest smoking rate in Canada. As part of this commitment, the government intends to take the necessary steps to increase fines on those convicted of selling tobacco to youth and to impose stronger sanctions for repeat offenders of Ontario’s tobacco- related laws. These sanctions would include prohibiting a retailer from selling tobacco products or lottery tickets and would be implemented by the fall. The availability of cheap, illegal tobacco makes it easier for non-smokers, especially youth, to start smoking, and removes an incentive for smokers to quit, undermining the government’s policies to reduce smoking. The government will work with key partners to further educate the public about health and social problems associated with tobacco and will undertake research to help measure the impact of its tobacco strategies on smoking levels in the province. Ontario has also committed to doubling enforcement efforts to address the supply of cheap, illegal tobacco. As part of this commitment, the government will focus on the implementation of additional regulatory, enforcement and other provisions in Bill 186, which was enacted in 2011. 258

answer.en: One 1987 Library of Parliament page says Health and Welfare Canada started anti-smoking campaigns aimed at youth and voiced concern about health costs from tobacco use. It says the federal government placed voluntary limits on tobacco advertising and kept giving money to tobacco farmers. It also says groups were pressing federal and provincial governments to act. The pages do not give any provincial government statement.
answer.fr: Une page de 1987 de la Bibliothèque du Parlement dit que Santé et Bien-être social Canada a lancé des campagnes contre le tabagisme destinées aux jeunes et s'est dit préoccupé par les coûts de santé liés au tabac. Elle dit que le gouvernement fédéral a mis des restrictions volontaires sur la publicité du tabac et a continué de subventionner les producteurs de tabac. Elle dit aussi que des groupes pressaient les gouvernements fédéral et provinciaux d'agir. Les pages ne donnent aucune déclaration d'un gouvernement provincial.

answer.en: A 1987 Library of Parliament paper says Health and Welfare Canada started anti-smoking campaigns aimed at youth. It also says the federal government placed voluntary restrictions on tobacco advertising while it continued to subsidize tobacco farmers. A 1989 Quebec overview sets a goal of cutting the number of smokers by 50% by the year 2000. The pages do not cover what other governments said.
answer.fr: Un document de 1987 de la Bibliothèque du Parlement indique que Santé et Bien-être social Canada a lancé des campagnes contre le tabagisme visant les jeunes. Il dit aussi que le gouvernement fédéral a imposé des restrictions volontaires à la publicité du tabac tout en continuant de subventionner les producteurs de tabac. Un aperçu de 1989 sur le Québec fixe l'objectif de réduire de 50 % le nombre de fumeurs d'ici l'an 2000. Les pages ne disent rien sur ce qu'ont dit les autres gouvernements.

answer.en: By 1991, the pages show federal and Quebec governments acting on tobacco. Health and Welfare Canada ran anti-smoking campaigns aimed at youth, and the federal government raised tobacco taxes and passed a 1989 Act on tobacco advertising. Quebec set a goal to reduce the number of smokers by 50% by the year 2000. The pages do not cover other provinces or what every government said.
answer.fr: En 1991, les pages montrent que le gouvernement fédéral et celui du Québec agissent au sujet du tabac. Santé et Bien-être social Canada a mené des campagnes antitabac visant les jeunes, et le gouvernement fédéral a haussé les taxes sur le tabac et adopté en 1989 une loi sur la publicité du tabac. Le Québec s'est fixé comme objectif de réduire de 50 % le nombre de fumeurs d'ici l'an 2000. Les pages ne couvrent pas les autres provinces ni tout ce que chaque gouvernement a dit.

answer.en: By 1992, the pages show governments acting on tobacco in several ways. Health and Welfare Canada ran anti-smoking campaigns aimed at youth, federal taxes on tobacco rose, and Parliament passed the Tobacco Products Control Act and the Non-Smokers' Health Act in 1988. Quebec set a goal to reduce the number of smokers. The pages do not give the full contents of these laws.
answer.fr: En 1992, les pages montrent que les gouvernements ont agi de plusieurs façons au sujet du tabac. Santé et Bien-être Canada a mené des campagnes contre le tabagisme visant les jeunes, les taxes fédérales sur le tabac ont augmenté, et le Parlement a adopté en 1988 la Loi réglementant les produits du tabac et la Loi sur la santé des non-fumeurs. Le Québec s'est fixé un objectif de réduction du nombre de fumeurs. Les pages ne donnent pas le contenu complet de ces lois.

answer.en: By 1992, federal pages say that Health and Welfare Canada ran anti-smoking campaigns aimed at youth, and that Parliament passed the Tobacco Products Control Act and the Non-Smokers' Health Act in 1988. A 1991 page says taxes on tobacco went up with every federal budget since the late 1980s. The pages do not show what governments said after 1992, and the 2001 page only lists references.
answer.fr: En 1992, les pages fédérales indiquent que Santé et Bien-être social Canada menait des campagnes anti-tabac visant les jeunes, et que le Parlement a adopté en 1988 la Loi réglementant les produits du tabac et la Loi sur la santé des non-fumeurs. Une page de 1991 dit que les taxes sur le tabac ont augmenté à chaque budget fédéral depuis la fin des années 1980. Les pages ne montrent pas ce que les gouvernements ont dit après 1992, et la page de 2001 ne contient qu'une liste de références.

answer.en: Two Library of Parliament papers, from 1987 and 1992, describe government action on tobacco. In 1987, Health and Welfare Canada had started anti-smoking campaigns for youth, while the federal government still helped tobacco farmers. The 1992 paper says Parliament passed the Tobacco Products Control Act and the Non-Smokers' Health Act in 1988. The pages do not give what those laws said.
answer.fr: Deux documents de la Bibliothèque du Parlement, de 1987 et de 1992, décrivent l'action des gouvernements sur le tabac. En 1987, Santé et Bien-être social Canada avait lancé des campagnes contre le tabagisme destinées aux jeunes, mais le gouvernement fédéral continuait d'aider les producteurs de tabac. Le document de 1992 indique que le Parlement a adopté en 1988 la Loi réglementant les produits du tabac et la Loi sur la santé des non-fumeurs. Les pages ne disent pas ce que ces lois prévoyaient.

answer.en: By 2011, a federal report said Canada's Tobacco Act regulates the making, sale, labelling and promotion of tobacco products. It described the Federal Tobacco Control Strategy as a joint effort to keep people, especially youth, from starting or continuing to smoke and to protect people from second-hand smoke. Earlier pages from 1987 and 1992 describe government concern about health costs and the passing of two laws in 1988. These pages do not give the full text of any law.
answer.fr: En 2011, un rapport fédéral indiquait que la Loi sur le tabac de Canada réglemente la fabrication, la vente, l'étiquetage et la promotion des produits du tabac. Il décrivait la Stratégie fédérale de lutte contre le tabagisme comme un effort commun pour empêcher les gens, surtout les jeunes, de commencer ou de continuer à fumer, et pour les protéger de la fumée secondaire. Des pages plus anciennes, de 1987 et de 1992, parlent de l'inquiétude des gouvernements face aux coûts de santé et de deux lois adoptées en 1988. Ces pages ne donnent le texte complet d'aucune loi.

answer.en: Federal pages say Canada has a Tobacco Act and a Federal Tobacco Control Strategy aimed at stopping people from starting or continuing to smoke, and at protecting people from second-hand smoke. Earlier pages say the federal government ran anti-smoking campaigns for youth and passed two laws in 1988. The pages do not list every law or statement by every government.
answer.fr: Des documents fédéraux indiquent que le Canada a une Loi sur le tabac et une Stratégie fédérale de lutte contre le tabagisme, visant à empêcher les gens de commencer ou de continuer à fumer et à les protéger de la fumée secondaire. Des documents plus anciens disent que le gouvernement fédéral a mené des campagnes antitabac pour les jeunes et adopté deux lois en 1988. Ces pages ne présentent pas toutes les lois ni toutes les déclarations de tous les gouvernements.
